executiveSummary: The most consequential development this period is the disruption of the "Eviltokens" phishing-as-a-service platform, which reportedly enabled compromise of more than 12,000 Microsoft accounts across over 10,000 organizations and scaled business email compromise (BEC) using AI-assisted lure customization and mailbox analysis. View Article Law enforcement in the United Kingdom arrested two suspects connected to the operation, underscoring escalating criminal misuse of AI to industrialize financially motivated social engineering. View Article In Brazil, election authorities tightened deepfake standards for political advertising following use of AI-generated endorsement content, creating immediate compliance obligations for campaigns, broadcasters, and platforms ahead of national voting. View Article Defensively, provenance and detection capabilities continue to evolve. Platforms expanded C2PA and AI-identification features to help users verify content, while updated guidance provides practical deployment paths for content credentials. View Article View Article At the same time, new research suggests provenance watermarking may inadvertently provide shortcuts that weaken some audio deepfake detectors, indicating detection stacks must be validated against such interactions. View Article Threat actors are also exploiting trusted AI platforms and search outputs to deliver malware or steer victims toward attacker infrastructure, amplifying the social-engineering surface around AI tools. View Article View Article Overall, the environment is assessed as worsening due to the demonstrated scale of AI-enabled BEC and persistent risks to election integrity despite emerging authenticity controls.
